t: You're looking at the tomb of Thomas Hood, in Kensington and Chelsea. Hood is buried here and commemorated by it. He was a poet and humorist, best known for The Bridge of Sighs and The Song of the Shirt, and he wrote regularly for Punch. He was never robust and died at forty-five. The monument was made by Matthew Noble, a leading Victorian portrait sculptor, whose work also appears in Westminster Abbey, St Paul's Cathedral and Parliament Square.
